card.name: Kathak
card.era: Roots in ancient storytellers/bhakti movement; flourished in Mughal courts
card.tagline: North India's storytelling classical dance of footwork and spins
card.profile: Kathak is one of the major Indian classical dance forms, its name derived from Kathakars ('storytellers') - traveling bards of ancient northern India who narrated Hindu epics through dance, song and music (Wikipedia). Textual studies suggest it began in Banaras (Varanasi) and spread to Lucknow, Jaipur and other regions, developing distinct gharanas that vary in emphasis on footwork versus expression (Wikipedia). It is known for rhythmic footwork, rapid spins (chakkars), expressive abhinaya and the tabla; under Mughal patronage it incorporated Persian and Urdu elements, making it the only Indian classical dance to feature Persian influences (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Marginalized during British rule through its association with nautch/tawaif performers, kathak was preserved via the guru-shishya system and gained formal recognition as a classical dance after Indian independence (Britannica).
